title: Go: ETL Data Pipeline
description: Build an ETL data pipeline in Go using io.Reader and io.Writer interfaces with composable pipeline stages.

steps.title: Extractor stage (source)
steps.description: Implement an `Extractor` that implements `io.Reader`. It reads from a `[]string` data source and returns data line by line. Implement the `Read(p []byte)` method. Create an extractor with sample CSV data and use `io.Copy(os.Stdout, extractor)` to print it.
hints: Extractor struct holds `data []string` and `pos int` to track current line
`Read` copies the next line into `p` and returns the byte count
Return `io.EOF` when all lines have been read

verification.successMessage: Extractor implements io.Reader and produces data line by line!
verification.failureMessage: Make sure io.Copy prints all lines from the extractor to stdout.

steps.title: Transformer with map/filter
steps.description: Implement a `Transformer` that wraps an `io.Reader` and transforms data on the fly. Support a `Map` function (e.g. uppercase all text) and a `Filter` function (e.g. skip empty lines). Chain them: read from the extractor, transform, and print the output.
hints: Transformer holds the underlying `reader io.Reader` and applies transformations via function fields
Read a line, apply Map function, then check Filter function before returning data
Functions can be of type `func(string) string` for Map and `func(string) bool` for Filter

verification.successMessage: Transformer correctly applies Map and Filter functions to the data stream!
verification.failureMessage: Print the transformed data — all text should be uppercase with empty lines removed.

steps.title: Loader stage (sink)
steps.description: Implement a `Loader` that implements `io.Writer`. It accumulates written data into a `[]string` slice. Implement `Write(p []byte)` to collect data. Connect the transformer to the loader and verify the accumulated data by printing each item.
hints: Loader struct has `data []string` protected by a mutex
Write splits input on newlines and appends non-empty strings to data
Provide a `GetData() []string` method to retrieve accumulated output

verification.successMessage: Loader correctly accumulates all written data into a slice!
verification.failureMessage: Print each item in the loader's accumulated data after writing.

steps.title: Pipeline chaining with error handling
steps.description: Create a `Pipeline` struct that chains extractor, transformer, and loader stages together with `Run()` method that returns an error. Use `io.Pipe` to connect stages. Implement a `Retry` decorator that retries a stage up to 3 times on failure. Print pipeline status at each stage.
hints: Use `io.Pipe()` to create synchronous in-memory pipes between stages
Run each stage in a separate goroutine and collect errors via a channel
The Retry decorator wraps a stage and retries with exponential backoff on error

verification.successMessage: Pipeline chains stages together with proper error handling and retry!
verification.failureMessage: Print 'Pipeline stage X complete' for each successful stage.

steps.title: Pipeline metrics and monitoring
steps.description: Extend the Pipeline with metrics collection. Implement a `Metrics` struct that tracks bytes processed, records processed, errors, and timing per stage using `time.Time`. After pipeline execution, print a metrics report with stage name, duration, records, and error count.
hints: Wrap each stage with a metrics-gathering decorator that records start/end time
Use `sync/atomic` for counters shared across goroutines
Print a formatted report: `fmt.Printf("[%s] %d records in %v\n", name, records, duration)`

verification.successMessage: Pipeline metrics accurately track records, bytes, errors, and timing per stage!
verification.failureMessage: Print a metrics report for each pipeline stage with records and duration.
